name: Turmeric
description: Bright yellow root used in South Asian cooking; one of the most studied anti-inflammatory foods, valued for its broad activity across multiple inflammatory pathways.

activeCompounds.name: Curcumin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits NF-κB pathway, reduces COX-2 expression, lowers TNF-α and IL-6 levels

tips.preparation: Use ground or fresh root; add to oil-based dishes for absorption
tips.bioavailability: Pair with black pepper (piperine) — increases absorption up to 2000%
tips.cautions: May interact with blood thinners; consult provider if on warfarin

name: Ginger
description: Aromatic root with established anti-inflammatory and antiemetic properties; especially useful for migraine and pain conditions.

activeCompounds.name: Gingerols
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis; modulates COX and LOX pathways

activeCompounds.name: Shogaols
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduces TNF-α and IL-6 production; antioxidant effects on lipid peroxidation

tips.preparation: Fresh root grated or sliced; or 1-2 g powdered
tips.bioavailability: Active compounds are heat-stable; absorption is good without enhancers
tips.cautions: May increase bleeding risk at high doses with anticoagulants

name: Wild Salmon
description: Fatty cold-water fish rich in long-chain omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA, with strong evidence for cardiovascular and autoimmune inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Competes with arachidonic acid for COX/LOX enzymes, shifting eicosanoid production toward less inflammatory mediators

activeCompounds.name: DHA (docosahexaenoic acid)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Precursor to resolvins and protectins, which actively resolve inflammation

tips.preparation: Wild-caught preferred; bake, grill, or pan-sear
tips.bioavailability: Cooking does not significantly degrade omega-3s; avoid deep-frying
tips.cautions: Some farmed varieties are higher in omega-6; check for sustainable sourcing

name: Blueberries
description: Deeply pigmented berries packed with anthocyanins; strong evidence for vascular and neurological inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce CRP and IL-6; protect endothelial cells from oxidative damage

activeCompounds.name: Pterostilbene
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates SIRT1 pathway and AMPK, improving cellular stress response

tips.preparation: Fresh or frozen — frozen retains anthocyanins well
tips.bioavailability: Wild blueberries have ~2x the anthocyanin content of cultivated
tips.cautions: No common interactions; high-fiber serving may be a trigger for some IBS patterns

name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
description: Unrefined olive oil rich in monounsaturated fats and polyphenols; foundational fat in the Mediterranean diet pattern.

activeCompounds.name: Oleocanthal
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes similarly to ibuprofen at much lower potency

activeCompounds.name: Hydroxytyrosol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; reduces oxidized LDL and lowers vascular inflammation markers

tips.preparation: Use unrefined; drizzle on cooked food rather than for high-heat frying
tips.bioavailability: Pair with vegetables to absorb fat-soluble compounds
tips.cautions: Quality varies significantly — choose first cold-pressed, dark-glass-bottled brands

name: Tart Cherries
description: Sour Montmorency cherries with high anthocyanin content; well-studied for exercise-related inflammation, gout, and sleep-related neurological benefit.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibit COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes; reduce CRP and uric acid

activeCompounds.name: Melatonin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Endogenous antioxidant; supports circadian-driven inflammation resolution

tips.preparation: Fresh, frozen, or unsweetened tart cherry juice concentrate
tips.dosage: 1 oz concentrate (or 1 cup whole cherries) once or twice daily
tips.bioavailability: Anthocyanins are heat-sensitive; concentrate retains them better than baked goods
tips.cautions: Juice is high in natural sugars; whole fruit is preferable for diabetics

name: Pomegranate
description: Ruby-seeded fruit with one of the highest polyphenol concentrations of any food; arils and juice both reduce vascular and joint inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: Punicalagins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Potent antioxidants; downregulate NF-κB and MMP-13 in cartilage

activeCompounds.name: Urolithins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Gut microbial metabolites of ellagitannins; enhance mitophagy and reduce systemic inflammation

tips.preparation: Eat arils whole or drink 100% juice without added sugar
tips.dosage: 1/2 cup arils or 4-8 oz juice daily
tips.bioavailability: Urolithin production depends on gut microbiome — effects vary between individuals
tips.cautions: Juice can interact with statins and blood pressure medications via CYP3A4

name: Strawberries
description: Red berries with a high vitamin C and anthocyanin profile; consistent evidence for lowering CRP and improving vascular function.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins (pelargonidin)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce oxidized LDL and CRP; improve endothelial function

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin C
activeCompounds.mechanism: Cofactor for collagen synthesis and antioxidant recycling

tips.preparation: Fresh or frozen — frozen is picked ripe and retains nutrients well
tips.bioavailability: Vitamin C is heat- and light-sensitive; eat raw when possible
tips.cautions: One of the higher-pesticide-residue conventional crops; choose organic when feasible

name: Raspberries
description: Bramble fruit rich in ellagitannins, a precursor to gut-derived urolithins with systemic anti-inflammatory effects.

activeCompounds.name: Ellagitannins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Gut microbiota convert these to urolithins, which reduce inflammation and improve mitochondrial function

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; protect endothelium and neural tissue

tips.preparation: Fresh or frozen; pair with full-fat yogurt or seeds
tips.bioavailability: Freezing actually breaks cell walls and may improve compound release
tips.cautions: Tiny seeds may be irritating in active diverticulitis

name: Blackberries
description: Dark-pigmented bramble fruit with one of the highest anthocyanin and ellagic acid contents among berries.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins (cyanidin)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce CRP and IL-6; protect endothelial cells

activeCompounds.name: Ellagic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; modulates NF-κB pathway

tips.preparation: Fresh or frozen; minimal processing preserves anthocyanins
tips.bioavailability: Color intensity correlates with anthocyanin content — choose deeply pigmented berries
tips.cautions: No common interactions

name: Oranges
description: Citrus fruit notable for vitamin C and the flavonoid hesperidin, which support vascular health and immune-mediated inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin C
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; cofactor in collagen synthesis and immune regulation

activeCompounds.name: Hesperidin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Flavonoid that reduces capillary fragility and lowers CRP

tips.preparation: Eat whole rather than juiced — fiber blunts glycemic response
tips.bioavailability: Hesperidin concentrates in the white pith — eat with some pith intact
tips.cautions: Citrus can trigger GERD; high acid may erode enamel if juiced

name: Pineapple
description: Tropical fruit and the dietary source of bromelain, a proteolytic enzyme with documented anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects.

activeCompounds.name: Bromelain
activeCompounds.mechanism: Proteolytic enzyme that reduces edema, modulates cytokines, and aids protein digestion

tips.preparation: Eat fresh — bromelain is destroyed by canning and prolonged heat
tips.dosage: 1 cup fresh pineapple daily, or supplement 200-500 mg bromelain
tips.bioavailability: Bromelain is most concentrated in the core; consume on empty stomach for systemic anti-inflammatory effect
tips.cautions: May increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants; can cause oral irritation

name: Papaya
description: Tropical fruit containing the proteolytic enzyme papain along with carotenoids that support digestion and skin health.

activeCompounds.name: Papain
activeCompounds.mechanism: Proteolytic enzyme that aids protein digestion and reduces gut inflammation

activeCompounds.name: Lycopene
activeCompounds.mechanism: Carotenoid antioxidant; protects skin and vasculature from oxidative stress

tips.preparation: Eat ripe; squeeze lime to enhance flavor and vitamin C synergy
tips.bioavailability: Papain is most active in unripe (green) papaya
tips.cautions: Avoid unripe papaya in pregnancy due to latex content; latex allergy cross-reactivity

name: Kiwi
description: Small green fruit with exceptional vitamin C density and the digestive enzyme actinidin; supports gut motility and antioxidant status.

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin C
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; supports collagen synthesis and immune regulation

activeCompounds.name: Polyphenols and actinidin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Aid protein digestion and reduce intestinal inflammation

tips.preparation: Eat with skin (well-washed) for additional fiber and polyphenols
tips.dosage: 2 kiwis daily — clinically studied for constipation relief
tips.bioavailability: Vitamin C is best preserved when eaten raw and unprocessed
tips.cautions: Cross-reactivity with latex and birch pollen allergies

name: Apples
description: Common pome fruit notable for quercetin in the skin and pectin fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

activeCompounds.name: Quercetin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Flavonoid that stabilizes mast cells and inhibits NF-κB-driven cytokine release

activeCompounds.name: Pectin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Soluble fiber fermented to short-chain fatty acids that reduce gut and systemic inflammation

tips.preparation: Eat with skin — quercetin is concentrated there
tips.bioavailability: Pair with nut butter to slow glycemic response
tips.cautions: Conventional apples carry high pesticide residues; choose organic when feasible

name: Broccoli
description: Cruciferous vegetable and the leading dietary source of sulforaphane, a potent activator of the body's endogenous antioxidant defenses.

activeCompounds.name: Sulforaphane
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 pathway, upregulating phase-2 detoxification enzymes and antioxidant defenses

tips.preparation: Lightly steam (3-4 minutes) to preserve sulforaphane while activating the enzyme myrosinase
tips.bioavailability: Sprinkle mustard seed powder or add a few radish slices to cooked broccoli to restore myrosinase activity
tips.cautions: High vitamin K can interfere with warfarin dosing

name: Kale
description: Dense leafy green packed with magnesium, vitamin K, carotenoids, and sulforaphane precursors; one of the most nutrient-dense foods available.

activeCompounds.name: Lutein and zeaxanthin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Carotenoids that protect neural and retinal tissue from oxidative damage

activeCompounds.name: Glucosinolates
activeCompounds.mechanism: Precursors to sulforaphane and indole-3-carbinol; modulate inflammatory and detoxification pathways

tips.preparation: Massage raw kale with olive oil and lemon, or lightly sauté with garlic
tips.bioavailability: Pair with healthy fats to absorb fat-soluble vitamins and carotenoids
tips.cautions: High vitamin K affects warfarin; high oxalates may aggravate kidney stones

name: Spinach
description: Tender leafy green and one of the highest dietary sources of magnesium, folate, and lutein, with relevance to migraine and vascular inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: Magnesium
activeCompounds.mechanism: Cofactor in over 300 enzymatic reactions; stabilizes vascular and neural membranes

activeCompounds.name: Folate
activeCompounds.mechanism: Lowers homocysteine, a vascular inflammation marker

tips.preparation: Briefly sauté or steam — wilting concentrates nutrients and reduces oxalate
tips.dosage: 1-2 cups raw or 1/2 cup cooked daily
tips.bioavailability: Cook spinach to reduce oxalates that bind minerals; pair with vitamin C for iron absorption
tips.cautions: High oxalates contraindicated in calcium-oxalate kidney stone formers

name: Swiss Chard
description: Colorful leafy green with thick stems; rich in magnesium and vitamin K and one of few greens supplying betalain pigments.

activeCompounds.name: Magnesium
activeCompounds.mechanism: Vascular and neural stabilization; reduces migraine susceptibility

activeCompounds.name: Betalains
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidants that inhibit COX-2 and reduce oxidative stress

tips.preparation: Sauté both leaves and stems with olive oil and garlic
tips.bioavailability: Briefly cooking improves magnesium and carotenoid availability while reducing oxalates
tips.cautions: High vitamin K affects warfarin dosing

name: Brussels Sprouts
description: Small cruciferous vegetable with high sulforaphane potential and dense vitamin K content; supports detoxification and joint health.

activeCompounds.name: Sulforaphane
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin K
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supports calcium metabolism and reduces vascular calcification

tips.preparation: Roast halved at 400°F until edges caramelize, or shred raw for slaws
tips.bioavailability: Roasting reduces bitterness without destroying most glucosinolates
tips.cautions: Can cause gas; high vitamin K affects warfarin

name: Red Cabbage
description: Purple-pigmented cruciferous vegetable that combines anthocyanins with sulforaphane precursors — uncommon among vegetables.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce CRP and improve endothelial function

activeCompounds.name: Sulforaphane
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway

tips.preparation: Eat raw in slaws, lightly braised, or fermented as sauerkraut
tips.bioavailability: Acidic dressings (vinegar, lemon) stabilize anthocyanins and deepen color
tips.cautions: No common interactions

name: Cauliflower
description: Mild cruciferous vegetable supplying sulforaphane and choline; lower compound density than broccoli but versatile and well-tolerated.

activeCompounds.name: Sulforaphane
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2; supports detoxification pathways

activeCompounds.name: Choline
activeCompounds.mechanism: Methyl donor; supports membrane integrity and reduces homocysteine

tips.preparation: Roast florets at high heat, or rice and use as a grain substitute
tips.bioavailability: Light steaming preserves more sulforaphane than boiling
tips.cautions: FODMAP-sensitive individuals may experience gas

name: Beets
description: Root vegetable rich in betalains and dietary nitrates that lower blood pressure and reduce muscle inflammation.

activeCompounds.name: Betalains
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibit COX-2; antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects in joint and vascular tissue

activeCompounds.name: Dietary nitrates
activeCompounds.mechanism: Convert to nitric oxide, improving endothelial function and exercise recovery

tips.preparation: Roast whole in skin, or drink fresh beet juice for highest nitrate dose
tips.dosage: 1 medium beet or 8 oz juice daily
tips.bioavailability: Nitrates are heat-stable; betalains are sensitive to long cooking
tips.cautions: May cause harmless red urine; high oxalates for stone formers

name: Carrots
description: Root vegetable rich in beta-carotene, the carotenoid precursor to vitamin A that supports skin and mucosal immunity.

activeCompounds.name: Beta-carotene
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant carotenoid; precursor to vitamin A for epithelial and immune function

activeCompounds.name: Falcarinol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Polyacetylene with anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet activity

tips.preparation: Lightly cook to break cell walls, then eat with fat for carotenoid absorption
tips.bioavailability: Cooking increases beta-carotene bioavailability by ~6x vs. raw
tips.cautions: Excess intake can cause harmless yellow-orange skin tint (carotenemia)

name: Bell Peppers
description: Sweet peppers with the highest vitamin C density of common vegetables; red varieties also supply capsanthin and beta-carotene.

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin C
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antioxidant; cofactor in collagen synthesis

activeCompounds.name: Capsanthin and capsorubin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Red carotenoids that protect skin and vascular tissue from oxidative damage

tips.preparation: Eat raw to maximize vitamin C, or roast to concentrate carotenoids
tips.bioavailability: Red peppers contain ~2x the vitamin C of green; pair with oil for carotenoid uptake
tips.cautions: Nightshade-sensitive individuals (rare) may experience joint flares

name: Sweet Potato
description: Starchy tuber rich in beta-carotene; purple varieties additionally supply anthocyanins for combined antioxidant effect.

activeCompounds.name: Beta-carotene
activeCompounds.mechanism: Vitamin A precursor; supports skin and mucosal immunity

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins (purple varieties)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce CRP; protect vasculature from oxidative damage

tips.preparation: Roast with skin on for fiber, or bake whole at 400°F
tips.bioavailability: Pair with fat (butter, olive oil) for carotenoid absorption
tips.cautions: Higher glycemic load than non-starchy vegetables

name: Tomatoes
description: Red fruit eaten as a vegetable; the leading dietary source of lycopene, a potent carotenoid antioxidant.

activeCompounds.name: Lycopene
activeCompounds.mechanism: Carotenoid antioxidant; reduces oxidized LDL and protects skin from UV damage

tips.preparation: Cooked tomatoes (sauce, paste) deliver more bioavailable lycopene than raw
tips.dosage: 1/2 cup cooked tomato sauce daily, or 1 large fresh tomato
tips.bioavailability: Heat breaks down cell walls and the fat in olive oil dramatically improves lycopene absorption
tips.cautions: Nightshade family — rare sensitivity may aggravate joint symptoms

name: Asparagus
description: Spring vegetable supplying glutathione, inulin fiber, and saponins that support gut and vascular health.

activeCompounds.name: Glutathione
activeCompounds.mechanism: Master endogenous antioxidant; protects against oxidative damage

activeCompounds.name: Inulin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria

tips.preparation: Steam or roast briefly to preserve glutathione
tips.bioavailability: Overcooking destroys glutathione; aim for 3-5 minute cook time
tips.cautions: Causes harmless sulfur-smelling urine in some individuals

name: Garlic
description: Pungent allium with organosulfur compounds that lower blood pressure, modulate immunity, and support gut microbial balance.

activeCompounds.name: Allicin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Released when garlic is crushed; antimicrobial and inhibits NF-κB

activeCompounds.name: Diallyl sulfides
activeCompounds.mechanism: Lipid-soluble organosulfur compounds with cardiovascular and immunomodulatory effects

tips.preparation: Crush or chop and let rest 10 minutes before cooking to maximize allicin formation
tips.bioavailability: Raw or briefly cooked is most potent; aged garlic extract has different but complementary actions
tips.cautions: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants; can cause heartburn and odor

name: Onions
description: Allium vegetable supplying quercetin and organosulfur compounds; one of the best whole-food sources of quercetin.

activeCompounds.name: Quercetin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Mast cell stabilizer; inhibits NF-κB-mediated cytokine release

activeCompounds.name: Organosulfur compounds
activeCompounds.mechanism: Support detoxification and cardiovascular function

tips.preparation: Red onions and shallots have the highest quercetin; eat raw or lightly cooked
tips.bioavailability: Quercetin is heat-stable; outer layers contain more compound than the core
tips.cautions: High FODMAP; may trigger IBS symptoms in sensitive individuals

name: Sardines
description: Small oily fish that combine the EPA/DHA profile of larger fatty fish with vitamin D, calcium, and a very low mercury burden.

activeCompounds.name: EPA and DHA
activeCompounds.mechanism: Compete with arachidonic acid; precursors to resolvins that actively resolve inflammation

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin D
activeCompounds.mechanism: Immunomodulator; supports regulatory T-cell function

tips.preparation: Canned in olive oil or water; eat the soft bones for calcium
tips.bioavailability: Among the lowest-mercury fish — short food chain and small size
tips.cautions: High purines; people with active gout should moderate intake

name: Mackerel
description: Oily fish among the densest sources of omega-3s; pick smaller varieties like Atlantic or Spanish mackerel to limit mercury.

activeCompounds.name: EPA and DHA
activeCompounds.mechanism: Resolvin and protectin precursors; reduce systemic inflammation

tips.preparation: Grill, broil, or smoke; pairs well with strong flavors like lemon and capers
tips.bioavailability: Atlantic and Spanish mackerel are low-mercury; avoid king mackerel which is high
tips.cautions: King mackerel has very high mercury and should be avoided in pregnancy

name: Anchovies
description: Tiny oily fish typically cured in salt or oil; deliver concentrated omega-3s with very low mercury exposure.

activeCompounds.name: EPA and DHA
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce inflammatory eicosanoids; precursors to specialized pro-resolving mediators

tips.preparation: Add to dressings, sauces, and pizza for umami flavor with omega-3 benefit
tips.bioavailability: Oil-packed retains omega-3s well; rinse salt-cured to reduce sodium
tips.cautions: High sodium content; people with hypertension should moderate intake

name: Pasture-Raised Eggs
description: Whole eggs from hens with access to pasture; superior omega-3 and carotenoid content compared to conventional eggs.

activeCompounds.name: Choline
activeCompounds.mechanism: Methyl donor and structural component of cell membranes; supports neural function

activeCompounds.name: Lutein and zeaxanthin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Carotenoids that protect retinal and neural tissue from oxidative damage

tips.preparation: Soft-cook or poach to preserve heat-sensitive nutrients in the yolk
tips.bioavailability: Most carotenoids and choline are in the yolk; cook gently to preserve them
tips.cautions: Some autoimmune patients react to egg whites (lysozyme); pasture-raised reduces but does not eliminate this

name: Oysters
description: Bivalve mollusks with the highest zinc density of any common food; also supply omega-3s, B12, and copper.

activeCompounds.name: Zinc
activeCompounds.mechanism: Cofactor in over 300 enzymes; essential for skin integrity and immune regulation

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin B12
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supports neural function and homocysteine clearance

tips.preparation: Raw on the half-shell, grilled, or in a stew; pair with lemon
tips.dosage: 6 oysters provides several days' worth of zinc
tips.bioavailability: Animal-source zinc is far more bioavailable than plant-source
tips.cautions: Risk of foodborne illness if raw — source from reputable suppliers; shellfish allergy

name: Bone Broth
description: Long-simmered stock from animal bones rich in collagen-derived peptides, glutamine, and minerals; traditional remedy for gut and joint health.

activeCompounds.name: Collagen peptides
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supply glycine and proline; support connective tissue and intestinal barrier

activeCompounds.name: Glutamine
activeCompounds.mechanism: Primary fuel for enterocytes; supports gut barrier function

tips.preparation: Simmer bones with vinegar for 12-24 hours; add vegetables and herbs in the last hour
tips.dosage: 1-2 cups daily, especially during gut healing protocols
tips.bioavailability: A splash of vinegar in the cooking water extracts more minerals from bone
tips.cautions: High histamine content may trigger symptoms in histamine-intolerant individuals

name: Cinnamon
description: Bark spice with documented effects on blood glucose, lipid profile, and vascular inflammation; choose Ceylon over Cassia for lower coumarin.

activeCompounds.name: Cinnamaldehyde
activeCompounds.mechanism: Improves insulin signaling; reduces postprandial inflammation and CRP

tips.preparation: Add to oatmeal, coffee, yogurt, or roasted vegetables
tips.bioavailability: Ceylon ('true') cinnamon is preferred for daily use; Cassia is much higher in coumarin
tips.cautions: Cassia cinnamon at high doses may stress the liver; can interact with diabetes medications

name: Cayenne
description: Ground hot chili pepper containing capsaicin, which acts on TRPV1 receptors to reduce pain signaling over time.

activeCompounds.name: Capsaicin
activeCompounds.mechanism: TRPV1 agonist; depletes substance P from sensory neurons, reducing nociceptive signaling

tips.preparation: Sprinkle on soups, eggs, and roasted vegetables
tips.bioavailability: Topical capsaicin creams (0.025-0.075%) are effective for localized arthritis and neuropathy pain
tips.cautions: Can aggravate GERD, ulcers, and hemorrhoids; topical use can cause burning

name: Black Pepper
description: Common kitchen spice whose alkaloid piperine dramatically enhances absorption of curcumin and other polyphenols.

activeCompounds.name: Piperine
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits glucuronidation in the liver, increasing systemic availability of other compounds

tips.preparation: Use freshly cracked; pre-ground loses volatile oils quickly
tips.bioavailability: Even a small pinch with curcumin boosts curcumin absorption by up to 2000%
tips.cautions: Piperine alters drug metabolism — may affect levels of medications cleared by glucuronidation

name: Cloves
description: Aromatic flower buds with the highest antioxidant capacity of common spices; eugenol provides analgesic and antimicrobial effects.

activeCompounds.name: Eugenol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits COX-2 and 5-LOX; topical analgesic and antimicrobial

tips.preparation: Use whole in stews, mulled drinks, or ground in baking
tips.bioavailability: Eugenol is volatile — store cloves whole and grind just before use
tips.cautions: Concentrated clove oil can irritate mucosa; can interact with anticoagulants

name: Rosemary
description: Mediterranean herb containing carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid with documented neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects.

activeCompounds.name: Carnosic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 pathway; protects neurons from oxidative damage

activeCompounds.name: Rosmarinic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits COX-2 and lipoxygenase; reduces complement activation

tips.preparation: Use fresh or dried in roasts, marinades, and infused oils
tips.dosage: 1 teaspoon dried daily, or several fresh sprigs
tips.bioavailability: Marinating meats with rosemary before high-heat cooking reduces formation of inflammatory carcinogens
tips.cautions: High doses may interact with anticoagulants and lithium

name: Oregano
description: Mediterranean herb with one of the highest phenolic contents among culinary herbs; carvacrol and thymol offer antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory action.

activeCompounds.name: Carvacrol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits NF-κB; broad antimicrobial activity against gut pathogens

activeCompounds.name: Thymol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antimicrobial; reduces oxidative stress

tips.preparation: Sprinkle dried oregano on pizza, pasta, and roasted vegetables
tips.dosage: 1 teaspoon dried daily, or oil of oregano supplement when targeted
tips.bioavailability: Oil of oregano is concentrated — use with food for short courses, not daily long-term
tips.cautions: Concentrated oil can irritate mucosa and may disrupt beneficial gut bacteria with prolonged use

name: Thyme
description: Mediterranean herb rich in thymol and rosmarinic acid; supports respiratory health, gut microbial balance, and skin.

activeCompounds.name: Thymol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antimicrobial; reduces oxidative stress in epithelial tissues

activeCompounds.name: Rosmarinic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits COX-2 and reduces inflammatory cytokines

tips.preparation: Add fresh or dried to soups, stews, and roasts
tips.bioavailability: Volatile oils are best preserved by adding thyme late in cooking
tips.cautions: Concentrated essential oil should not be ingested undiluted

name: Sage
description: Mediterranean herb with traditional use for cognitive support; rosmarinic acid and carnosol provide neuroprotective effects.

activeCompounds.name: Rosmarinic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits acetylcholinesterase and reduces neuroinflammation

activeCompounds.name: Carnosol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway

tips.preparation: Use fresh in butter sauces, or dried in stuffings and meat rubs
tips.dosage: 1 teaspoon dried daily, or fresh leaves brewed as tea
tips.bioavailability: Sage tea (1 cup, 2x daily) has been studied for cognitive support
tips.cautions: Avoid high-dose sage essential oil — thujone content can be neurotoxic; avoid in pregnancy

name: Basil
description: Aromatic herb used culinarily and medicinally; sweet basil and holy basil both supply eugenol and ursolic acid with adaptogenic and anti-inflammatory effects.

activeCompounds.name: Eugenol
activeCompounds.mechanism: Inhibits COX-2 and reduces inflammatory eicosanoids

activeCompounds.name: Ursolic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduces NF-κB activation; supports glucose and lipid metabolism

tips.preparation: Add fresh basil at the end of cooking; holy basil (tulsi) is commonly drunk as tea
tips.dosage: Several fresh leaves daily, or 1-2 cups tulsi tea
tips.bioavailability: Volatile compounds are heat-sensitive; tear rather than chop to preserve them
tips.cautions: Holy basil may lower blood sugar and interact with diabetes medications

name: Parsley
description: Common herb that doubles as a vegetable in larger amounts; particularly rich in apigenin, vitamin K, and vitamin C.

activeCompounds.name: Apigenin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Flavonoid that downregulates NF-κB and reduces inflammatory cytokines

activeCompounds.name: Vitamin K
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supports calcium metabolism and reduces vascular calcification

tips.preparation: Use generously as a salad green (tabbouleh) or as a garnish for vibrant color
tips.bioavailability: Italian (flat-leaf) parsley has stronger flavor and slightly higher phenolic content than curly
tips.cautions: High vitamin K may interfere with warfarin dosing

name: Oats
description: Whole grain rich in soluble beta-glucan fiber and unique avenanthramide polyphenols with vascular and skin anti-inflammatory effects.

activeCompounds.name: Beta-glucan
activeCompounds.mechanism: Soluble fiber that binds cholesterol and feeds beneficial gut bacteria

activeCompounds.name: Avenanthramides
activeCompounds.mechanism: Polyphenols unique to oats; reduce skin inflammation and vascular oxidative stress

tips.preparation: Choose rolled or steel-cut over instant; soak overnight for easier digestion
tips.bioavailability: Colloidal oatmeal applied topically also reduces eczema and skin inflammation
tips.cautions: Cross-contamination with gluten common — choose certified gluten-free if celiac

name: Quinoa
description: Gluten-free pseudocereal that supplies complete protein along with quercetin and kaempferol flavonoids.

activeCompounds.name: Quercetin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Mast cell stabilizer; inhibits NF-κB

activeCompounds.name: Complete protein profile
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supplies all essential amino acids supporting tissue repair

tips.preparation: Rinse before cooking to remove bitter saponins; toast briefly in oil for flavor
tips.bioavailability: Soaking overnight reduces antinutrients and improves mineral absorption
tips.cautions: Saponins on the outer layer can irritate the gut if not rinsed

name: Brown Rice
description: Whole-grain rice retaining bran and germ; supplies magnesium, fiber, and lignans absent in white rice.

activeCompounds.name: Magnesium
activeCompounds.mechanism: Cofactor in vascular and neural function; reduces inflammation markers

activeCompounds.name: Insoluble fiber
activeCompounds.mechanism: Supports regular bowel transit and feeds gut microbiota

tips.preparation: Soak before cooking; consider pressure cooking for digestibility
tips.bioavailability: Soaking and rinsing reduces both phytic acid and inorganic arsenic content
tips.cautions: Higher arsenic exposure than other grains — rotate with quinoa, buckwheat, and oats

name: Buckwheat
description: Gluten-free pseudocereal high in rutin, a flavonoid that strengthens capillaries and supports vascular and neural health.

activeCompounds.name: Rutin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Flavonoid that reduces capillary fragility and inhibits platelet aggregation

activeCompounds.name: Magnesium
activeCompounds.mechanism: Vascular and neural stabilizer; reduces migraine susceptibility

tips.preparation: Cook groats as a porridge, or use buckwheat flour for pancakes and soba noodles
tips.bioavailability: Toasting groats (kasha) deepens flavor without destroying rutin
tips.cautions: Despite the name, contains no wheat; rare cases of buckwheat allergy exist

name: Barley
description: Ancient whole grain particularly rich in beta-glucan fiber; consistently lowers LDL cholesterol and improves glycemic control.

activeCompounds.name: Beta-glucan
activeCompounds.mechanism: Soluble fiber that lowers cholesterol and feeds beneficial gut bacteria

activeCompounds.name: Lignans
activeCompounds.mechanism: Phytoestrogens with cardiovascular and anti-inflammatory effects

tips.preparation: Use hulled (whole) barley in soups, salads, and pilafs; avoid pearled which loses most fiber
tips.bioavailability: Beta-glucan is preserved through cooking; soaking shortens cook time
tips.cautions: Contains gluten — not suitable for celiac or gluten-sensitive individuals

name: Avocado
description: Tree fruit eaten as a fat source; the dominant source of monounsaturated oleic acid in produce, with carotenoids and fiber adding to its anti-inflammatory profile.

activeCompounds.name: Oleic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Monounsaturated fat that reduces oxidized LDL and dampens inflammatory gene expression

activeCompounds.name: Lutein
activeCompounds.mechanism: Carotenoid antioxidant protecting retinal and neural tissue

tips.preparation: Eat ripe and raw; spread on toast, slice into salads, or blend into smoothies
tips.bioavailability: Adding avocado to a salad increases absorption of carotenoids from other vegetables by 2-15x
tips.cautions: Latex-fruit cross-reactivity; high potassium for advanced kidney disease

name: Flaxseed Oil
description: Cold-pressed oil from flax seeds; one of the richest plant sources of ALA omega-3 fatty acid.

activeCompounds.name: Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Plant omega-3; partially converts to EPA/DHA and shifts eicosanoid balance

activeCompounds.name: Lignans
activeCompounds.mechanism: Phytoestrogens with anti-inflammatory and hormonal balancing effects

tips.preparation: Use cold — drizzle on salads, finished dishes, or blend into smoothies; never heat
tips.bioavailability: Conversion of ALA to EPA/DHA is limited (~5-10%); pair with marine omega-3 for fuller effect
tips.cautions: Highly oxidation-prone; store refrigerated in dark glass and use within weeks of opening

name: Walnut Oil
description: Cold-pressed oil from walnuts; supplies ALA omega-3 with the polyphenol profile of walnuts in a more concentrated form.

activeCompounds.name: Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Plant omega-3; supports vascular and neural inflammation resolution

activeCompounds.name: Walnut polyphenols
activeCompounds.mechanism: Ellagitannins and their gut metabolites (urolithins) reduce systemic inflammation

tips.preparation: Use unheated in salad dressings or drizzled on finished dishes
tips.bioavailability: Heat destroys ALA and walnut polyphenols; never use for cooking
tips.cautions: Oxidizes quickly; refrigerate and discard if it smells bitter or paint-like

name: Coconut Oil
description: Tropical saturated fat dominated by medium-chain fatty acids; evidence is mixed and effects vary by individual lipid response.

activeCompounds.name: Medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Rapidly absorbed and used as energy; may support ketone production for neurological function

activeCompounds.name: Lauric acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Antimicrobial against some gut pathogens; effects on cardiovascular markers are mixed

tips.preparation: Use for medium-heat cooking; topical use can support skin barrier
tips.dosage: 1-2 tablespoons daily, treated as a fat source not a daily must-have
tips.bioavailability: Virgin (unrefined) preserves polyphenols; refined has higher smoke point
tips.cautions: Raises LDL cholesterol in many individuals; use as part of a varied fat profile rather than as the dominant fat

name: Green Tea
description: Unoxidized tea leaves brewed as an infusion; one of the most consistently studied anti-inflammatory beverages, with effects across vascular, neural, and immune systems.

activeCompounds.name: EGCG (epigallocatechin gallate)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Catechin polyphenol that inhibits NF-κB, reduces oxidative stress, and modulates immune cell signaling

activeCompounds.name: L-theanine
activeCompounds.mechanism: Amino acid that promotes calm alertness and modulates inflammatory cytokine response to stress

tips.preparation: Steep at 175°F for 2-3 minutes; overheating produces bitter astringent compounds
tips.bioavailability: Adding a squeeze of lemon increases catechin stability and absorption
tips.cautions: Contains caffeine; can reduce iron absorption — drink between meals if iron-deficient

name: Matcha
description: Powdered Japanese green tea consumed as a suspension of whole leaf; delivers concentrated EGCG and L-theanine relative to brewed green tea.

activeCompounds.name: EGCG (concentrated)
activeCompounds.mechanism: Whole-leaf consumption delivers 3-10x the catechin dose of steeped green tea

activeCompounds.name: L-theanine
activeCompounds.mechanism: Promotes calm focus and dampens stress-induced inflammatory signaling

tips.preparation: Whisk 1 tsp into 6 oz hot (not boiling) water until frothy
tips.bioavailability: Ceremonial-grade matcha has higher L-theanine; culinary grade is fine for daily use
tips.cautions: Higher caffeine per serving than steeped tea; may interact with stimulant medications

name: Rooibos Tea
description: Caffeine-free South African herbal infusion with a unique flavonoid profile; suitable for evening use and sensitive individuals.

activeCompounds.name: Aspalathin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Flavonoid unique to rooibos that improves glucose regulation and reduces oxidative stress

activeCompounds.name: Nothofagin
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduces vascular inflammation and improves endothelial function

tips.preparation: Steep 1 tsp loose tea in boiling water for 5-7 minutes
tips.bioavailability: Green (unfermented) rooibos has higher aspalathin than the more common red (fermented) variety
tips.cautions: Generally well-tolerated; rare estrogenic effects with very high intake

name: Hibiscus Tea
description: Tart red herbal infusion from Hibiscus sabdariffa flowers; clinical trials show modest but consistent blood pressure reduction.

activeCompounds.name: Anthocyanins
activeCompounds.mechanism: Reduce vascular oxidative stress and improve endothelial function

activeCompounds.name: Hibiscus acids
activeCompounds.mechanism: Mild ACE-inhibitor activity contributing to blood pressure reduction

tips.preparation: Steep dried calyces in hot water 5-10 minutes; enjoy hot or iced
tips.dosage: 2-3 cups daily, studied for blood pressure benefit
tips.bioavailability: Cold-brewing for 1-2 hours extracts anthocyanins gently and reduces tartness
tips.cautions: May enhance the effect of antihypertensive medications; can interact with chloroquine

name: Coffee (in moderation)
description: Roasted coffee bean infusion; the largest source of antioxidants in the typical Western diet, with documented neurological and metabolic benefits at moderate doses.

activeCompounds.name: Chlorogenic acid
activeCompounds.mechanism: Phenolic antioxidant; improves glucose handling and reduces inflammatory markers

activeCompounds.name: Caffeine
activeCompounds.mechanism: Adenosine receptor antagonist; supports alertness and reduces neuroinflammation at moderate doses

tips.preparation: Filter coffee preferred — paper filters trap cafestol/kahweol diterpenes that raise LDL
tips.dosage: 2-4 cups daily; beyond that, benefits plateau and adverse effects increase
tips.bioavailability: Light roasts retain more chlorogenic acid; dark roasts have a slightly different antioxidant profile
tips.cautions: Can trigger anxiety, palpitations, GERD, or migraine in sensitive individuals; avoid after early afternoon for sleep
